tytul: Roasted parsnip purée preserved by tyndallization: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for roasted parsnip purée preserved in jars by tyndallization, that is, by heating the jars several times with pauses.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Pressure canning is the only recommended method for canning meat, poultry, seafood and vegetables; using a boiling-water bath for these foods poses a real risk of botulism poisoning.
NCHFP says not to try canning puréed vegetables, red meats or poultry at home, because proper processing times for puréed foods have not been determined for home use.
Tyndallization (repeated heating with pauses for spores to germinate) is not considered fully reliable, because some superdormant spores do not germinate between heatings.

akapity: Botulinum spores are very hard to destroy at boiling-water temperatures.
JarAtlas has found no tested home recipe for parsnip purée in jars from a checked source.
